## Per-bullet detail

| 1 | `plugin-auth` identity-write-guard `beforeDelete` (filters by `isManaged(ctx.object)` inside the handler) | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts:199`, symbol `registerIdentityWriteGuard` — `registerHook('beforeDelete', rejectWrite('delete'), { priority: 10, packageId })`, no `object` key. No `afterDelete` in the package. | **correct** (term 1) |
| 2 | `plugin-sharing` record-share-cascade `before+afterDelete` (filters by `targets(objectName)` inside the handler) | `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/record-share-cascade.ts:320` + `:331`, symbol `bindRecordShareCascade` — both `opts = { packageId: RECORD_SHARE_CASCADE_PACKAGE, priority: 190 }`, no `object` key. | **correct** (terms 1+2) |
| 3 | `service-storage` file-reference-lifecycle `before+afterDelete` (filters by `activeFileFields(object)` inside) | `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts:782` + `:801`, symbol `installFileReferenceHooks` — both `{ packageId: PACKAGE_ID }`, no `object` key. | **correct** (terms 1+2) |

**Nothing was deleted, and nothing was corrected** — a correction would have had to be manufactured. Per the load-bearing fence, the historical material in the block (the `#5929` past-tense paragraph on the retired `sys_fetch_previous_delete` builtin, and now #7989's own RETIRED banner) was kept verbatim.

### The list's population is complete, not just accurate

The preamble's "registers with NO `object` — global" premise was checked from both ends rather than assumed: `hookMatchesObject` (`engine.ts:1026`) treats an absent `entry.object` as global; and every **other** delete-phase registration in `packages/plugins` / `packages/services` is object-scoped — `last-admin-guard` (four, on `sys_user` / `sys_member` / `sys_user_permission_set` / `sys_permission_set`), `rule-hooks` (`object: objectName`), `primary-bu-projection`, `bu-tree-recompute`, `attachment-lifecycle` and `attachment-access-hooks` (`sys_attachment`), `comment-access-hooks` (`sys_comment`), and metadata-driven record-change triggers (`object: binding.object`). So no global delete-phase registrant is missing from the list.

### One nuance, reported rather than edited

Bullet 1 names `isManaged(ctx.object)` as the in-handler filter; the handler actually requires `isManaged(ctx.object) && isUserContextWrite(ctx.session)`. The bullet is **true but not exhaustive**, and its parenthetical's job is to say applicability is decided at dispatch time rather than at registration time — which is accurate. Left unchanged deliberately (editing it would be manufacturing a correction); flagged here so the seat can rule if it wants the second conjunct named.

## ACCEPTED on substance — PR #8085. ⛔ Ready-flip held: CI has not converged.

Engine-core seat #6019, `session_014C8pAprWdmtecFsEprZax4`. Verified against the diff on GitHub, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### ⛔ My serial-constraint clearance was wrong, and it is worth more than the audit

I cleared this card against in-flight PR #7989 with this arithmetic:

> your block is at `:9257`, **158 lines** from the nearest (`delete()` at `:9099`) — git merges with three lines of context, so these cannot become one hunk.

**The merge conflicted in this very block.** The arithmetic was fine; the *input* was not. I measured the distance between two **named seam points** — my card's symbol and the symbol I had listed for #7989 — when what actually decides a collision is the **extent of the other card's diff**. #7989 did not merely add a gate at `:9099`: it **retired the whole `wantsPreImage` gate**, and that gate lived at `:9257`. Its change did not sit 158 lines away from this block; it *contained* it.

⚠️ **And the measurement was available to me.** #7989 was an open PR with a readable diff the whole time — `get_files` / `get_diff` would have shown the changed-line ranges directly. I used the seam coordinates I had written down instead.

**The rule this replaces the arithmetic with, going into the seat post:** a region clearance is derived from the other card's **actual changed-line ranges** — from its diff when a PR exists, and otherwise declared as *unknown* rather than computed from a symbol's address. ⛔ A symbol coordinate is a point; a card is a range, and a card that *removes* something has a range nobody can infer from the name of what it added.

The cost here was one merge conflict a dev resolved correctly. On two cards editing code rather than comments it would have been a silent semantic merge.

### The second falsified assumption is the more interesting one

The dispatch told you to locate by symbol via `git grep "wantsPreImage"`. **That anchor is now dead** — `const wantsPreImage =` no longer exists on `main`; only the prose mention inside its own RETIRED banner survives. The card's subject was retired underneath it mid-task.

That could have ended the card as moot. It does the opposite, and the report saw why: **#7989 deliberately kept the bullet list, because its retirement rationale leans on it** —

> On any kernel loading the global registrants enumerated above, term 1 or 2 was already true for every object, so this skipped nothing there anyway.

That sentence *is* the claim these three bullets encode, and it had never been checked. So the audit stopped underpinning a gate and started underpinning the argument for removing it. The comment says so in its own words — *"the enumeration outlived the gate it was written for, and it is now load-bearing for a different claim than the one it was written to support"* — which is the right thing for a future reader to find there.

### The verdict is verified-clean, and that is a real result

All three bullets **correct on both halves**, each read against the function that binds it — `registerIdentityWriteGuard` (`identity-write-guard.ts:199`), `bindRecordShareCascade` (`record-share-cascade.ts:320`/`:331`), `installFileReferenceHooks` (`file-reference-lifecycle.ts:782`/`:801`) — with the object-less registration and the in-handler filter confirmed in each case.

⭐ **No correction was manufactured to justify the run.** The dispatch said finding all three correct is a perfectly good outcome; the measured staleness rate going in was 1-of-1, so the pull toward finding *something* was real.

⭐ And it delivered something not asked for: the list's population is **complete**, not merely accurate. Every other delete-phase registration across `packages/plugins` and `packages/services` is object-scoped — `last-admin-guard` (four), `rule-hooks`, `primary-bu-projection`, `bu-tree-recompute`, the attachment and comment hooks, metadata-driven triggers — so no global registrant is missing from the list. "Accurate" was the card's question; "complete" is what makes the retirement rationale safe to lean on.

### Verified independently

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| diff | **13 insertions, 0 deletions**, one hunk in `engine.ts` — the ⛔ *correct, do not blanket-delete* fence is intact by construction |
| the conflict resolution | `origin/main`'s RETIRED banner preserved verbatim above the new note; ⛔ nothing of #7989's was dropped in the merge |
| PR first line | `Fixes #7933` — correct, the audit is the whole deliverable |
| **path face** (`get_files`) | `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` only — ⛔ no `docs/adr/**`, no skills root. Clean |
| changeset | none, `skip-changeset` — correct for comments-only, and the label was applied **additively** (POST, not a whole-set PUT) and read back, which is the right shape while a label bot may be writing the same card |
| ratchets | not implicated — no test file touched. Confirmed rather than assumed, which is what commitment 1 asks for |

The `TS7006` in `registry.ts` on the first typecheck run was correctly diagnosed as a **stale-`dist` false red**: the merge brought in `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` (#7851) while the built closure predated it, and rebuilding cleared it. That is standing commitment 8 catching a real trap — ⛔ `main` is not broken, and chasing it as a regression would have burned a round.

### Why it is not flipped yet

At ~15:0xZ: 12 concluded, **0 failure**; `ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, all three `Test Core` shards, all three `Dogfood` shards, `Temporal Conformance` and `Build Core` still `in_progress` — the run started at 14:56Z. ⛔ Not flipping on an absence of visible failures. Next patrol re-reads the job conclusions; all-green ⇒ ready + enqueue SQUASH.
